name: lantern_bay
revision: r2 (2026-11-10): the r1 critic's and continuity's must-fixes applied (reviews/r1-response.md). Grandma is MAE. The reveal now flips 'never came back': the chest proves Grandpa got there.
caption: why is grandma lighting the bottom of the sea 🏮
logline: Every night a boy's grandma swims out over a road of lanterns on the bay floor and adds one more; tonight he places the last one, and its light finds the chest Grandpa left for her on the shipwreck he never came back from: proof he got there.
question: why tf are there 300 lanterns on the bottom of the sea?
premise: A line of 300 lanterns glows on the floor of a bay, running straight out from the dock. Every night, when she thinks the boy is asleep, Grandma swims out over it, puts one more at the end and sprints home from the drowned that come out of the dark. She says it's a road (he thinks: for fish). He once swam to the end at noon: past the last lantern the deep is pitch black even by day, with tridents in it, and nothing is ever in the lit part (lucky water, he thinks). One night Grandpa dove to the shipwreck out there for Grandma's present and never came back. His boat, the MAE, never came back either.
twist: The lanterns are a road across water nobody can cross in the dark: drowned only spawn where the block light is 0, and 13 blocks down the sky light is 2 even at noon, so the deep bay is deadly day and night unless you light it. Grandma has built the road one lantern a night to the shipwreck where Grandpa went for her present. Tonight the boy places the last lantern on the wreck's bow; the light finds a chest on the deck, and the chest screen's title reads FOR MAE (a renamed chest), a Heart of the Sea inside. Grandpa got there. He found her present and, with the drowned coming, locked it in a chest with her name on it (items he carried would have despawned; a chest keeps them forever). 'He never came back' becomes 'he got there': the road she built leads to proof he made it.
